item.title: Silverrudder 2025
item.description:
Chasing the Silverrudder: One Sailor’s Solo Voyage around Fyn
#

By the time September 2025 arrived, I had been dreaming of this moment for years – a single-handed circumnavigation of Fyn in the famous Silverrudder Regatta. It sounded deceptively simple: 134 nautical miles around a Danish island in the Baltic, alone and without a stop. But anyone who sails knows what that really means: at least thirty hours at sea, at the mercy of wind, current, and your own endurance.

item.title: Classic Channel Regatta 2026
item.description:
What it is about
#

This race is all about spirited, seamanlike sailing across the English Channel in style and forging new friendships along the way. Most of the yachts and crews are likely to hail from the UK and France, giving the whole event a distinctly Anglo-French flavour. And … Lucy is one of the pre-registered boats! Have a look for yourself at https://www.classic-channel-regatta.eu

item.title: Leg: Classic Channel
item.description:
Yeah, it’s regatta from 7 to 16 July 😎

The course of the Classic Channel Regatta 2026 runs from Dartmouth in the UK via St Peter Port in Guernsey and Lézardrieux in Brittany to Paimpol in Brittany, with races in between and a final circuit round Île de Bréhat.

Course description
#

The regatta starts with two race days off Dartmouth, followed by a crossing to St Peter Port. After that comes a race to Lézardrieux, a sail to Paimpol, and it finishes with the race round Île de Bréhat. The course covers about 150 nautical miles across the Channel.

item.title: Double Rundt 2025
item.description:
A Co32 battle flag was recently spotted flying the evening before the Double Rundt race, where a sailor completed the 32-nautical-mile course solo.

While the race is typically double-handed, the sailor onboard “Lucy” navigated the course alone. Photos taken in Langballigau Harbour after the race show the Co32 battle flag displayed on the boat.

“It was pretty breezy, and with the No2 genoa and full main, I had a bit too much sail up,” the commented Karsten. “But Lucy kept me safe, and I finished in good time.” Good to see.
